title: Ethereal Aperture — Cara, experimental and analog photography
description: Student work, classes, current experiments, exhibitions, and notes from Cara's life around analog photography.

about.pull: I teach classes where the camera is allowed to misbehave.
paragraphs: I started with a borrowed camera and no idea what I was doing, which turned out to be the right way in. A friend showed me how to develop a roll in a kitchen sink, and the part that stayed with me wasn't the picture — it was watching something appear that I had only partly controlled. I've worked in analog ever since, mostly black-and-white, mostly at home or in shared darkrooms.

Now I re-develop old prints, shoot film long past its date, and make photographs without a camera at all. The work is slow and a fair amount of it fails. I keep the failures that are more interesting than what I intended.

I teach in and around Cleveland — darkroom evenings, weekend workshops, and occasional sessions at community spaces in the region. Classes are small. We start with what the process actually does rather than with rules, and everyone prints. If you've never touched film, that's a fine place to begin; if you've been printing for years, there's usually something in the class that misbehaves in a new way.

My photographs have appeared in the Halide Project publication, at an analog photography festival in Pittsburgh, and in regional group shows. I'd rather the classes and the student work speak for the teaching, so I keep this part short.

artistStatement.pull: I'm less interested in a perfect image than in what happens when the process slips, doubles back, or makes its own decisions.
artistStatement.note: Most of what I make now starts as a mistake I decide to keep. I re-develop old prints, leave film in the wrong places, and let the chemistry work longer than it should.
